newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia peso dips on Occidental security problems.
newsitem.headline: Colombia peso dips on Occidental security problems.

text.p: Colombia's peso dipped 1.5 to 1,100.7 against the dollar Wednesday amid speculation caused by production problems facing U.S. multinational Occidental Petroleum Corp.

Occidental declared force majeure in its Cano Limon field in eastern Colombia Tuesday after a spate of leftist rebel attacks on the pipeline that connects the field to the Caribbean coast lifting terminal at Covenas.

"There was speculation pushing the peso down because of the Occidental news. There was also demand for dollars from the vehicle assembly business and some banks were looking to build up positions," one dealer said.

Some dealers said speculation on the back of the security problems facing Occidental, which normally produces 180,000 barrels a day from Cano Limon, could affect the market for as much as three months. The company is losing an estimated $4 million a day while production is halted.
The peso opened at 1,099.2, its intraday high, and sank to a low of 1,103.8. Dealers reported 497 trades worth an above- average $231 million.
